en.content:
Consider the following compound (X)

The most stable and least stable carbon radicals, respectively, produced by homolytic cleavage of corresponding bond are :

options.content: III, II
II, IV
I, IV
II, I

en.explanation:
Removing H from each labelled carbon of gives four carbon radicals.

Radical II is secondary and propargylic: the unpaired electron on C-II is delocalised into the adjacent bond by resonance, so it is the most stable.

Radical III is tertiary and is stabilised only by hyperconjugation and the effect of the alkyl groups, which is weaker than resonance; radical IV is primary and less stable still.

Radical I is formed on the carbon of the terminal alkyne. The unpaired electron occupies an orbital (50% -character) that lies along the axis, perpendicular to both bonds, so it cannot be delocalised; the C–H bond is also the strongest C–H bond in the molecule. Radical I is therefore the least stable.

Stability order: II > III > IV > I, so the most and least stable radicals are II and I.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

निम्नलिखित यौगिक पर विचार करें :

संगत आबन्ध के समापघटनी विदलन के कारण निर्मित सर्वाधिक स्थायी एवं न्यूनतम स्थायी कार्बन मूलक क्रमशः हैं :

options.content: III, II
II, IV
I, IV
II, I

hi.explanation:
के प्रत्येक अंकित कार्बन से H हटाने पर चार कार्बन मूलक प्राप्त होते हैं।

मूलक II द्वितीयक तथा प्रोपार्जिलिक है : C-II पर अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉन अनुनाद द्वारा संलग्न आबन्ध पर विस्थानीकृत हो जाता है, अतः यह सर्वाधिक स्थायी है।

मूलक III तृतीयक है और केवल अतिसंयुग्मन तथा ऐल्किल समूहों के प्रभाव से स्थायित्व पाता है, जो अनुनाद से दुर्बल है; मूलक IV प्राथमिक है और इससे भी कम स्थायी है।

मूलक I टर्मिनल ऐल्काइन के कार्बन पर बनता है। अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉन कक्षक (50% -गुण) में होता है जो अक्ष के अनुदिश है और दोनों आबन्धों के लम्बवत् है, अतः यह विस्थानीकृत नहीं हो सकता; साथ ही C–H आबन्ध अणु का सबसे प्रबल C–H आबन्ध है। इसलिए मूलक I सबसे कम स्थायी है।

स्थायित्व क्रम : II > III > IV > I, अतः सर्वाधिक तथा न्यूनतम स्थायी मूलक क्रमशः II और I हैं।

अतः, सही विकल्प (D) है।

en.explanation:
Radii (pm): metallic radius Al 143, Ga 135; ionic radius 53.5, 62.

Statement I: Ga has ten 3d electrons, which shield the nuclear charge poorly, so its outer electrons feel a larger effective nuclear charge and its metallic radius (135 pm) is smaller than that of Al (143 pm). Statement I is incorrect.

Statement II: () has one more electron shell than (), so (53.5 pm) is smaller than (62 pm). Statement II is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

Given below are two statements :

Statement (I) : In octahedral complexes, when high spin complexes are formed. When low spin complexes are formed.

Statement (II) : In tetrahedral complexes because of , low spin complexes are rarely formed.

options.content: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

en.explanation:
In octahedral complexes, which have a coordination number (CN) of 6, the formation of high spin or low spin complexes depends on the relative magnitude of the crystal field splitting energy, denoted as Δ₀, and the pairing energy (P.E.):

If Δ₀ is less than the pairing energy (Δ₀ < P.E.), high spin complexes are formed.

If Δ₀ is greater than the pairing energy (Δ₀ > P.E.), low spin complexes are formed.

In tetrahedral complexes, where the coordination number is 4:

The crystal field splitting energy (Δₜ) is typically less than the pairing energy (Δₜ < P.E.), resulting in the formation of mainly high spin complexes. Low spin complexes are rarely observed in tetrahedral coordination due to this energy consideration.

en.content:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : Vanilin will react with NaOH and also with Tollen's reagent.

Statement II : Vanilin will undergo self aldol condensation very easily.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.content: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

en.explanation:
Vanillin is 4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde. Its phenolic is acidic, so it reacts with NaOH to form the sodium phenoxide, and its group is oxidised by Tollens' reagent, depositing silver. Statement I is correct.

Self aldol condensation requires an -hydrogen, on the carbon next to the carbonyl group, to form an enolate. In vanillin the group is attached directly to a ring carbon that carries no hydrogen, so no enolate forms and vanillin cannot undergo self aldol condensation. Statement II is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

options.content: All naturally occurring amino acids except glycine contain one chiral centre.
Amino acid, cysteine can easily undergo dimerisation due to the presence of free SH group.

Glutamic acid is the only amino acid that contains a <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.186ex;" width="1.76ex" height="1.505ex" role="img" viewBox="0 -583 778 665"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g><g><use href="#MJX-TEX-N-2212"/></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>COOH group at the side chain.
All naturally occurring amino acids are optically active.

en.explanation:
To clarify the statements regarding amino acids:

Chirality in Amino Acids: Most naturally occurring amino acids contain at least one chiral center, but there are exceptions. For example, Isoleucine has two chiral centers, and Glycine is an exception as it is optically inactive due to lacking a chiral center.

Cysteine and Dimerization: The amino acid Cysteine can easily undergo dimerization. This is due to its free sulfhydryl (SH) group, which can form disulfide bonds, leading to the formation of a dimer.

Carboxyl Groups in Amino Acids: Glutamic acid is not the only amino acid with a carboxyl group in its side chain. Aspartic acid also contains a carboxyl group in its side chain.

Optical Activity: While many naturally occurring amino acids are indeed optically active, Glycine is an exception as it does not possess a chiral center and is hence optically inactive.

In summary:

Not all naturally occurring amino acids are optically active (e.g., Glycine).

Not all naturally occurring amino acids contain only one chiral center (e.g., Isoleucine has two).

Both Glutamic acid and Aspartic acid contain side chain carboxyl groups.

Cysteine can dimerize due to its SH group.

ऐमीनो अम्ल सिस्टीन मुक्त SH समूह की उपस्थिति के कारण आसानी के साथ द्वितयीकरण कर सकता है।
ग्लूटैमिक अम्ल एकमात्र ऐमीनो अम्ल है जिसकी पार्श्व शृंखला में एक -COOH समूह उपस्थित है।
सभी प्राकृतिक रूप से उपलब्ध ऐमीनो अम्ल ध्रुवक घूर्णक होते हैं।

hi.explanation:
अमीनो अम्लों के संबंध में कथनों को स्पष्ट करने के लिए:

अमीनो अम्लों में चिरलता: अधिकांश प्राकृतिक रूप से पाए जाने वाले अमीनो अम्लों में कम से कम एक चिरल केंद्र होता है, लेकिन कुछ अपवाद हैं। उदाहरण के लिए, Isoleucine में दो चिरल केंद्र होते हैं, और Glycine एक अपवाद है क्योंकि चिरल केंद्र की अनुपस्थिति के कारण यह प्रकाशिक रूप से निष्क्रिय है।

सिस्टीन और द्विभवन: अमीनो अम्ल Cysteine आसानी से द्विभवन से गुजर सकता है। यह इसके मुक्त सल्फहाइड्रिल (SH) समूह के कारण होता है, जो डाइसल्फाइड बंध बना सकता है, जिससे एक द्विलक का निर्माण होता है।

अमीनो अम्लों में कार्बोक्सिल समूह: Glutamic acid एकमात्र अमीनो अम्ल नहीं है जिसकी पार्श्व श्रृंखला में कार्बोक्सिल समूह होता है। Aspartic acid में भी इसकी पार्श्व श्रृंखला में कार्बोक्सिल समूह होता है।

प्रकाशिक सक्रियता: जबकि कई प्राकृतिक रूप से पाए जाने वाले अमीनो अम्ल वास्तव में प्रकाशिक रूप से सक्रिय होते हैं, Glycine एक अपवाद है क्योंकि इसमें चिरल केंद्र नहीं होता है और इसलिए यह प्रकाशिक रूप से निष्क्रिय है।

सारांश में:

सभी प्राकृतिक रूप से पाए जाने वाले अमीनो अम्ल प्रकाशिक रूप से सक्रिय नहीं होते हैं (उदाहरण के लिए, Glycine)।

सभी प्राकृतिक रूप से पाए जाने वाले अमीनो अम्लों में केवल एक ही चिरल केंद्र नहीं होता है (उदाहरण के लिए, Isoleucine में दो होते हैं)।

Glutamic acid और Aspartic acid दोनों में पार्श्व श्रृंखला कार्बोक्सिल समूह होते हैं।

Cysteine अपने SH समूह के कारण द्विभवन कर सकता है।

en.explanation:
In water the basic strength of an amine is set by three effects together: the effect of the alkyl groups, hydrogen-bond solvation of the protonated amine, and steric hindrance to that solvation.

For ethyl amines the larger effect of three ethyl groups outweighs the poorer solvation of , so the aqueous order is (pKb 3.00, 3.25, 3.29). This differs from the methyl series, where is stronger than .

All three ethyl amines are stronger bases than (pKb 4.75), whose nitrogen carries no electron-releasing group.

In hydrazine, , the electronegative group withdraws electron density from the other nitrogen ( effect), so hydrazine (pKb about 6) is a weaker base than ammonia.

Option (B) places below , which is the methyl-series pattern and does not apply to ethyl amines.

Note: NTA's answer key for this question gives (B), with . The NCERT pKb values above make triethylamine the stronger base of the two, so (C) is kept.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

en.explanation:
All four compounds are propanoyl derivatives , and hydrolysis is nucleophilic acyl substitution: water adds to the C=O carbon and leaves. The rate rises as becomes a weaker base (better leaving group) and as resonance donation from L into the C=O falls.

Basicity of the leaving groups: (conjugate base of the strong acid HCl) < ( of ) < ( of ) < ( of ).

Resonance donation into the carbonyl increases in the same direction: Cl donates least, the anhydride oxygen shares its lone pair between two C=O groups, the ester oxygen donates more, and the amide nitrogen donates most, making the amide carbonyl the least electrophilic.

So the order is acid chloride (p) > anhydride (q) > ester (r) > amide (s).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
